name: Norwegian stev (solo singing-game)
lineage: Norwegian stev solo-singing tradition of inland-Norway (Setesdal, Telemark, and adjacent mountain regions), comprising short improvised-or-traditional four-line quatrains sung unaccompanied. Two main streams: gamlestev ("old stev") canonical fixed-traditional-stanzas, and nystev ("new stev") improvised-on-occasion stanzas often performed in competitive-dialogic exchange between two singers. Performance: solo unaccompanied voice in characteristic narrow-range Norwegian-pentatonic-and-modal vocabulary with strict stev-meter four-stress-line. The Hilme inland-Norway lineage and the canonical nineteenth-century stev-singers (Jorunn Hilme, Talleiv Røysland) consolidated institutional documentation; the post-1970s Norwegian folk-music revival re-established practice.
